question: Should OpenClaw preserve ref-scoped failures for existing Vault tokens denied `auth/token/lookup-self`, or intentionally require that capability and treat those all-403 batches as provider outages?
rationale: A Vault 403 from self-lookup is ambiguous between an unavailable/revoked token and an otherwise valid token without introspection permission, so documentation alone cannot determine whether changing established runtime classification is acceptable.

options.title: Preserve lookup-denied compatibility
options.body: Treat failed self-lookup as inconclusive and keep the prior ref-scoped result unless a shared provider outage can be established without requiring a new token capability.

options.title: Adopt the explicit introspection contract
options.body: Require `auth/token/lookup-self` for no-default-policy tokens and accept provider-scoped diagnostics when that capability is absent.

recommendation.title: Preserve lookup-denied compatibility
recommendation.body: Treat failed self-lookup as inconclusive and keep the prior ref-scoped result unless a shared provider outage can be established without requiring a new token capability.

likelyOwner.reason: The current implementation and linked bug report establish the proposed Vault behavior and its compatibility tradeoff.
